greek: Καὶ ηὐλόγησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν Νωε καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε καὶ πληρώσατε τὴν γῆν καὶ κατακυριεύσατε αὐτῆς.
hint: God blesses Noah and his sons with the words of 1:28.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *pĕrû ûrĕbû ûmilʾû ʾet-hāʾāreṣ*, *be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth*, and stops. The Greek adds *and gain dominion over it*, the last command of 1:28.
The first sense in the passive, as at 8:17: αὐξάνω *to make large*, πληθύνω *to make full*; the passives' own *to grow* and *to prevail* stand last in the chains.
κατακυριεύω has one sense in Middle Liddell, *to gain dominion over*, so it is plain text.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: And [[spoke well of|spoke well of, praised, honoured, blessed]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[name:Νωε]] and the sons of him and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] to them [[be made large|be made large, be increased and augmented, be increased in power and strengthened and exalted, be promoted to honour and glorified and magnified, grow and wax and increase, grow up]] and [[be made full|be made full, be increased, be multiplied, be in the majority, prevail]] and [[make full|make full, fill full of, fill full, gorge and satiate, glut, fill with, man, make complete, fill, fulfil and pay in full and make up, come in full]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] and gain dominion over it.

names.gloss: (Νωε, from Hebrew Nōaḥ, usually connected with nûaḥ, "to rest")

greek: καὶ ὁ τρόμος ὑμῶν καὶ ὁ φόβος ἔσται ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς θηρίοις τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ κινούμενα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἰχθύας τῆς θαλάσσης· ὑπὸ χεῖρας ὑμῖν δέδωκα.
hint: The fear of man falls on every creature, given under his hands.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *môraʾăkem wĕḥittĕkem*, *the fear of you and the dread of you*. τρόμος is *a trembling, quaking*; φόβος is first *flight*, its only sense in Homer, and *fear* after it.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕyedkem nittānû*, *into your hand they are given*, passive. The Greek has God speak, *under hands to you I have given*, in the perfect: a gift that stands.
ὑπό with the accusative: Middle Liddell's first sense for that case is *towards and under*, motion that ends beneath. The phrase is the idiom *into your power*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out the last ἐπί.

greek: καὶ πᾶν ἑρπετόν, ὅ ἐστιν ζῶν, ὑμῖν ἔσται εἰς βρῶσιν· ὡς λάχανα χόρτου δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὰ πάντα.
hint: Every living creeping thing is given for food, as the green plants were.

notes.text: *As garden-herbs of grass*: the Hebrew *kĕyereq ʿēśeb*, *as the green plant*, looking back to the food given at 1:29–30.
The neuter plural used as a noun, *all things*, with the article: *the all things*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἔδωκα, the aorist; the perfect is the Berlin papyrus's, 911.

greek: πλὴν κρέας ἐν αἵματι ψυχῆς οὐ φάγεσθε·
hint: Only flesh with its blood is withheld.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bāśār bĕnapšô dāmô*, *flesh with its life, its blood*. The Greek has *flesh in blood of life*, and κρέας, *meat*, where the flesh of 6:12 and 6:17 was σάρξ.
Without a genitive πλήν is an adverb, and its first sense so used is *but*; *except, save* is the preposition's.

reading: [[but|but, than, much like, only not, except that, save that, except, save so far as, more than, save, short of]] [[flesh|flesh, meat, a piece of meat, dressed meat, a body and person]] [[in blood|within, inside of, and by means of blood, bloodshed and murder, race and kinship]] [[of breath|of breath, of the life, of the spirit, of life and death, of the ghost, of the departed soul]] not [[you will eat|you will eat, you will eat of]];

greek: καὶ γὰρ τὸ ὑμέτερον αἷμα τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν ἐκζητήσω, ἐκ χειρὸς πάντων τῶν θηρίων ἐκζητήσω αὐτὸ καὶ ἐκ χειρὸς ἀνθρώπου ἀδελφοῦ ἐκζητήσω τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
hint: God will require a man's life of beast and brother.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has two phrases, *miyyad hāʾādām miyyad ʾîš ʾāḥîw*, *from the hand of man, from the hand of each man's brother*. The Greek has one, *from hand of man, of brother*.
ἐκζητέω, *to seek out*, and *to demand an account of*. Luke 11:50–51 joins it to the verb of 9:6: ἵνα ἐκζητηθῇ τὸ αἷμα πάντων τῶν προφητῶν τὸ ἐκκεχυμένον … ἀπὸ αἵματος Ἅβελ.

notes.lemma: τὸ ὑμέτερον αἷμα τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν
notes.text: *Your blood, that of your lives*: the possessive adjective and the pronoun both, as the Hebrew *dimkem lĕnapšōtêkem*.

greek: ὁ ἐκχέων αἷμα ἀνθρώπου ἀντὶ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ ἐκχυθήσεται, ὅτι ἐν εἰκόνι θεοῦ ἐποίησα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
hint: Blood for blood, because man was made in God's likeness.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *šōpēk dam hāʾādām bāʾādām dāmô yiššāpēk*, *whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed*. The Greek has no *by man*: *the one pouring out blood of a man, over against his blood, will be poured out*.
[[flag]] *I made*: the Hebrew is *ʿāśâ*, *he made*, of God in the third person.
The Hebrew *bĕṣelem ʾĕlōhîm*, the phrase of 1:27, where the Greek had κατʼ εἰκόνα θεοῦ.
ἐκχέω, *to pour out*, in the future passive; the entry's own senses for the passive, from *to stream out* to *to lie languidly*, stand last.
Middle Liddell gives ἀντί first as *over against, opposite*, then *instead of*, *at the price of, for*. Perseus's summary and the senses for compounds are left out.

greek: ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε καὶ πληρώσατε τὴν γῆν καὶ πληθύνεσθε ἐπʼ αὐτῆς.
hint: The blessing again, with the earth to fill.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *širṣû bāʾāreṣ*, *swarm on the earth*. The Greek has *make full the earth*, the words of 9:1.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

hint: God speaks to Noah and his sons.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *ʾel-nōaḥ*, *to Noah*; the Greek has the dative.

greek: Ἐγὼ ἰδοὺ ἀνίστημι τὴν διαθήκην μου ὑμῖν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι ὑμῶν μεθʼ ὑμᾶς
hint: The covenant is raised up with Noah and the seed after him.

notes.text: *I make to stand up*: Middle Liddell gives ἀνίστημι its causal senses in the present, and its intransitive ones, *to stand up*, in the second aorist ἀνέστη of 4:8. The Hebrew *mēqîm* is the causative of *qûm*, *to stand*, and the Greek matches it stem for stem.
The word of 6:18. Middle Liddell's first sense is *a disposition* of property *by will*; *covenant* is its last.

greek: καὶ στήσω τὴν διαθήκην μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ οὐκ ἀποθανεῖται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἔτι ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι κατακλυσμὸς ὕδατος τοῦ καταφθεῖραι πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν. —
hint: No flood of water will destroy the earth again.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕlōʾ-yikkārēt kol-bāśār*, *all flesh shall not be cut off*. The Greek has *will not die off*.
[[flag]] *A deluge of water*: the Hebrew has *mabbûl* alone.
The words of 6:18, for the Hebrew *wahăqimōtî ʾet-bĕrîtî*.
Rahlfs prints a dash after the verse, closing a section.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyōʾmer ʾĕlōhîm*, *and God said*. The Greek adds κύριος, and *to Noah*.
The Hebrew *lĕdōrōt ʿôlām*. αἰώνιος is first *lasting for an age*, from αἰών, then *everlasting, eternal*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

notes.text: τόξον is *a bow*, the archer's weapon, the bow of Revelation 6:2; the Hebrew *qešet* is the same word for both. The rainbow of Revelation 4:3 and 10:1 is ἶρις.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *nātattî*, *I have set*; the Greek has the present, *I set*.

reading: [[the bow|the bow, the bow and arrows, the rays]] of me [[I set|I set, I put, I place, I plant, I lay]] [[in the cloud|within, inside of, and by means of the cloud, the bird-net]], and it will be [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[a sign|a sign, a mark and token, a sign from the gods and an omen, a signal, a standard and ensign, a boundary]] [[of a disposition|of a disposition of property by will, of a will and testament, of an arrangement between two parties, of a covenant]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] of me and [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῷ συννεφεῖν με νεφέλας ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ὀφθήσεται τὸ τόξον μου ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ,

notes.text: *In my collecting clouds*: συννεφέω, *to collect clouds*, with its cognate object, as the Hebrew *bĕʿanănî ʿānān*. ἐν joins the articular infinitive as it joins any object, and the infinitive's subject, με, follows as *of me*, as αὐτούς did at 4:8.
The future passive of ὁράω, *to see*: *will be seen*, the verb of 8:5.

hint: God will remember the covenant, and the water will not wipe out all flesh.

notes.text: μιμνήσκομαι, the verb of 8:1, with the covenant: the phrase of Luke 1:72, μνησθῆναι διαθήκης ἁγίας αὐτοῦ.
The Hebrew is *lĕšaḥēt*, *to destroy*, as at 9:11, where the Greek had καταφθεῖραι. Here it has ἐξαλείφω, *to plaster*, then *to wipe out*: the verb of 7:4 and 7:23.
Used as a conjunction with the infinitive, so the first conjunction sense, *so as to*; *as, as being* is the adverb's.

greek: καὶ ἔσται τὸ τόξον μου ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ, καὶ ὄψομαι τοῦ μνησθῆναι διαθήκην αἰώνιον ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον πάσης ψυχῆς ζώσης ἐν πάσῃ σαρκί, ἥ ἐστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: God will see the bow and remember the covenant lasting for an age.

notes.text: [[flag]] *Between me*: the Hebrew is *bên ʾĕlōhîm*, *between God*, in the third person.
The genitive article with the infinitive, of purpose: *I will see, to remind myself*. The Hebrew *ûrĕʾîtîhā lizkōr* has *I will see it*; the Greek has no object.

reading: and will be [[the bow|the bow, the bow and arrows, the rays]] of me [[in the cloud|within, inside of, and by means of the cloud, the bird-net]], and [[I will see|I will see, I will perceive, I will behold, I will look at]] [[to remind oneself of|to remind oneself of, to call to mind, to remember, to bethink oneself of, to be minded, to bear in mind and not forget]] [[a disposition|a disposition of property by will, a will and testament, an arrangement between two parties, a covenant]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting, eternal]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] of me and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of breath|of breath, of the life, of the spirit, of life and death, of the ghost, of the departed soul]] [[of living|of living, of alive, of in full life and strength, of fresh and strong]] [[in all|within, inside of, and by means of all, the whole, every, every single]] [[flesh|flesh, the flesh, muscles, the body, man's nature generally]], which is [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς τῷ Νωε Τοῦτο τὸ σημεῖον τῆς διαθήκης, ἧς διεθέμην ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον πάσης σαρκός, ἥ ἐστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: The covenant God disposed: the noun and its own verb.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾăšer hăqimōtî*, *which I have established*, the verb of 9:9 and 9:11. The Greek has διατίθεμαι, the verb διαθήκη is made from: *the disposition which I disposed*. Acts 3:25 has the same pair, τῆς διαθήκης ἧς διέθετο ὁ θεός.

Filed under the active διατίθημι. The entry's senses for the middle, *B. Mid.*, open *to arrange as one likes, to dispose of*; *to make a covenant with* is the fourth. The actives are left out, as for other verbs filed under their middle. Hebrews 9:16–17 calls a testator ὁ διαθέμενος.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] to [[name:Νωε]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[the sign|the sign, the mark and token, the sign from the gods and the omen, the signal, the standard and ensign, the boundary]] [[of the disposition|of the disposition of property by will, of the will and testament, of the arrangement between two parties, of the covenant]], which [[I arranged as I liked|I arranged as I liked, I disposed of, I disposed of my property and devised it by will, I set out for sale and disposed of, I arranged mutually, I made a covenant with, I settled with]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] of me and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of flesh|of flesh, of the flesh, of muscles, of the body, of man's nature generally]], which is [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: Ἦσαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Νωε οἱ ἐξελθόντες ἐκ τῆς κιβωτοῦ Σημ, Χαμ, Ιαφεθ· Χαμ ἦν πατὴρ Χανααν.
hint: The three sons of Noah, and Ham the father of Canaan.

notes.text: The Hebrew *wĕḥām hûʾ ʾăbî kĕnāʿan*. ἦν of a standing relation, with the state formula of 1:2.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.
Hebrew *Kĕnaʿan*; the New Testament names the land Χανάαν (Acts 7:11, 13:19).

reading: were, and kept on being, [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], the sons of [[name:Νωε]] [[the ones having gone out of|the ones having gone out of, having come out, having gone away and marched off, having gone forth]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of the wooden box|of the wooden box, of the chest, of the coffer]] [[name:Σημ]], [[name:Χαμ]], [[name:Ιαφεθ]]; [[name:Χαμ]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[father|father, grandfather]] of [[name:Χανααν]].

names.gloss: (Χαμ, from Hebrew Ḥām, usually connected with ḥam, "hot")
(Ιαφεθ, from Hebrew Yepet, which 9:27 ties to pātâ, "to make wide")
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: τρεῖς οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Νωε· ἀπὸ τούτων διεσπάρησαν ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν.
hint: From the three the whole earth is peopled.

notes.lemma: ἀπὸ τούτων διεσπάρησαν ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ûmēʾēlleh nāpĕṣâ kol-hāʾāreṣ*, *and from these the whole earth was spread abroad*: the earth is the subject. The Greek has *from these they were scattered abroad upon all the earth*.
The aorist passive of διασπείρω, *to scatter abroad*, the verb of the dispersion in Acts 8:1 and 8:4.

reading: three [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] are the sons of [[name:Νωε]]; [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of these|of these, of the nearer, of what follows]] [[were scattered abroad|were scattered abroad, were thrown about, were squandered]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]].

greek: Καὶ ἤρξατο Νωε ἄνθρωπος γεωργὸς γῆς καὶ ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα.
hint: Noah, a husbandman, plants a vineyard.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyāḥel nōaḥ ʾîš hāʾădāmâ*, *and Noah, a man of the ground, began*. The Greek has *a man, a husbandman of earth*, and like the Hebrew gives *began* no infinitive.
Used as a noun, so the first noun sense, *a husbandman*; the adjective, *tilling the ground*, follows in the chain. ἀμπελών, *a vineyard*, has one sense and is plain text.

reading: And [[began|began, made a beginning, made a beginning of, began from]] [[name:Νωε]] [[man|a man, a human being]] [[a husbandman|a husbandman, one tilling the ground]] [[of earth|of earth, of land, of the ground]] and [[planted|planted, planted for himself, begot, produced and brought about and caused]] a vineyard.

greek: καὶ ἔπιεν ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου καὶ ἐμεθύσθη καὶ ἐγυμνώθη ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Noah drinks the wine and lies uncovered in his house.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕtôk ʾohŏlōh*, *inside his tent*. The Greek has *in his house*.
μεθύσκω is *to make drunk*, and Middle Liddell files the aorist passive ἐμεθύσθην under it: *was made drunk*, with the passive's own *to get drunk* last.
γυμνόω, *to strip naked*, in the passive. The Hebrew *wayyitgal* is reflexive, *he uncovered himself*; the entry gives the passive that sense too, and it is in the chain.
οἶνος, *wine*, one sense, is plain text.

reading: and [[drank|drank, drank of, drank up]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] of the wine and [[was made drunk|was made drunk, was intoxicated and inebriated, was given to drink and watered and moistened, drank freely, got drunk, was drunk]] and [[was stripped naked|was stripped naked, was stripped, was left naked and exposed, was left bare and defenceless, stripped himself naked]] [[in the house|within, inside of, and by means of the house, the abode and dwelling, the room and chamber, the house of a god and temple, the household goods and substance, the household and family]] of him.

greek: καὶ εἶδεν Χαμ ὁ πατὴρ Χανααν τὴν γύμνωσιν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἀνήγγειλεν τοῖς δυσὶν ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ ἔξω.
hint: Ham sees his father's nakedness and tells his brothers.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew, which has *wayyaggēd lišnê-ʾeḥāyw baḥûṣ*, *and told his two brothers outside*. The Greek adds *having gone out*.
γύμνωσις, *a stripping*, then *nakedness*, from γυμνόω of 9:21; the Hebrew *ʿerwâ*.

reading: and [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at]] [[name:Χαμ]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather]] of [[name:Χανααν]] [[the stripping|the stripping, the nakedness, the defenceless side]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather]] of him and [[having gone out of|having gone out of, having come out, having gone away and marched off, having gone forth]] [[carried back tidings of|carried back tidings of, reported]] to the two [[to sons of the same mother|to sons of the same mother, to brothers, to near kinsmen]] of him [[out|out, out of, outside, without, foreign, clear of, beyond and over, but and except]].

greek: καὶ λαβόντες Σημ καὶ Ιαφεθ τὸ ἱμάτιον ἐπέθεντο ἐπὶ τὰ δύο νῶτα αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπορεύθησαν ὀπισθοφανῶς καὶ συνεκάλυψαν τὴν γύμνωσιν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν, καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν ὀπισθοφανές, καὶ τὴν γύμνωσιν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν οὐκ εἶδον.
hint: Shem and Japheth walk backwards and cover their father.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿal-šĕkem šĕnêhem*, *upon the shoulder of the two of them*. The Greek has *the two backs of them*.
The aorist middle of ἐπιτίθημι. Middle Liddell's *B. Mid.* opens *to put on oneself* or *for oneself*, and the form takes the first sense in its own voice; the actives are left out.

Neither is in Middle Liddell. LSJ gives the adjective *seen from behind*, then *looking backwards*, citing this verse for πρόσωπον, and the adverb one sense, *backwards*, citing it again; the adverb is plain text. The clause *and their face backward* has no verb.
συγκαλύπτω, *to cover* or *veil completely*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐπέθηκαν, the active.

reading: and [[having taken|having taken, having received, having taken hold of and grasped and seized]] [[name:Σημ]] and [[name:Ιαφεθ]] [[the outer garment|the outer garment, the cloak and mantle, the Roman toga, the clothes, the cloth]] [[put on themselves|put on themselves, put on for themselves, set themselves to and applied themselves to and employed themselves on, made an attempt upon and attacked, brought on themselves, caused to be imposed, laid commands on, gave]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] the two [[backs|backs, wide surfaces, plains, ridges]] of them and [[were driven|were driven, were carried, went, walked, marched, went across and passed]] backwards and [[covered|covered, veiled completely]] [[the stripping|the stripping, the nakedness, the defenceless side]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather]] of them, and [[the face|the face, the visage, the countenance, the look, the mask, the outward appearance]] of them [[seen from behind|seen from behind, showing behind, appearing behind or after, reversing the image, looking backwards]], and [[the stripping|the stripping, the nakedness, the defenceless side]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather]] of them not [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at]].

greek: ἐξένηψεν δὲ Νωε ἀπὸ τοῦ οἴνου καὶ ἔγνω ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ νεώτερος,
hint: Noah becomes sober and learns what his younger son did.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyîqeṣ*, *and he awoke*. The Greek has ἐκνήφω, *to sleep off a drunken fit, become sober again*.
The comparative of νέος, *young*: *the younger*, for the Hebrew *haqqāṭān*, *the small, the youngest*.

reading: [[slept off a drunken fit|slept off a drunken fit, became sober again]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Νωε]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] of the wine and [[learned to know|learned to know, perceived, marked, learned, discerned and distinguished]] [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as]] [[made|fashioned, wrought, produced, performed, did]] to him the son of him [[the younger|the younger, the more youthful, the newer and fresher, the stranger]],

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ἐπικατάρατος Χανααν· παῖς οἰκέτης ἔσται τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.
hint: The curse falls on Canaan.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿebed ʿăbādîm*, *a servant of servants*. The Greek has two nouns side by side, *a child, a house-slave*.
Middle Liddell's first sense is *a child*, in relation to descent; *a slave, servant* is its third, in relation to condition.
*Yet more accursed*, the one sense of 3:14, plain text.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] yet more accursed [[name:Χανααν]]; [[a child|a child, a son, a daughter, a grandchild, a boy and youth and lad, a girl and maiden, a slave and servant and man and maid]] [[a house-slave|a house-slave, a menial]] will be [[to the sons of the same mother|to the sons of the same mother, to the brothers, to the near kinsmen]] of him.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Σημ, καὶ ἔσται Χανααν παῖς αὐτοῦ.
hint: Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: the opening of the Benedictus.

notes.lemma: Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Σημ
notes.text: The Hebrew *bārûk YHWH ʾĕlōhê šēm*. The same words open Zechariah's song in Luke 1:68, Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ. εὐλογητός has one sense, *blessed*, and is plain text.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *wîhî*, *and let … be*, a wish. The Greek has the future, *will be*, and *of him* for the Hebrew *lāmô*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] blessed [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] of [[name:Σημ]], and will be [[name:Χανααν]] [[a child|a child, a son, a daughter, a grandchild, a boy and youth and lad, a girl and maiden, a slave and servant and man and maid]] of him.

greek: πλατύναι ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ιαφεθ καὶ κατοικησάτω ἐν τοῖς οἴκοις τοῦ Σημ, καὶ γενηθήτω Χανααν παῖς αὐτῶν.
hint: May God widen Japheth: the Hebrew name's play on the verb is lost.

notes.text: The aorist optative, a wish. The Hebrew *yapt ʾĕlōhîm lĕyepet* plays the verb *pātâ*, *to make wide*, against the name *Yepet*; πλατύνω, *to widen*, keeps the sense and loses the play.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾohŏlê-šēm*, *in the tents of Shem*. The Greek has *houses*, as at 9:21.
κατοικέω's first translation, *to dwell in as a κάτοικος*, leaves its last word in Greek; the headword stops at *dwell in*.

reading: [[may widen|may widen, may make wide]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] to [[name:Ιαφεθ]] and [[let dwell in|let dwell in, let settle in, let colonise, let inhabit, let settle and dwell, let lie and be situate]] [[in the houses|within, inside of, and by means of the houses, the abodes and dwellings, the rooms and chambers, the houses of a god and temples, the household goods and substances, the households and families]] of [[name:Σημ]], and [[let come into being|let come to be, let arise, let be brought into existence]] [[name:Χανααν]] [[a child|a child, a son, a daughter, a grandchild, a boy and youth and lad, a girl and maiden, a slave and servant and man and maid]] of them.

greek: Ἔζησεν δὲ Νωε μετὰ τὸν κατακλυσμὸν τριακόσια πεντήκοντα ἔτη.
hint: Noah lives three hundred and fifty years after the flood.

notes.text: The Hebrew *šĕlōš mēʾôt šānâ waḥămiššîm šānâ*; the numbers agree.

reading: [[lived|lived, was in full life and strength, was fresh and strong]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Νωε]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[the deluge|the deluge, the inundation]] three hundred fifty years.

greek: καὶ ἐγένοντο πᾶσαι αἱ ἡμέραι Νωε ἐννακόσια πεντήκοντα ἔτη, καὶ ἀπέθανεν.
hint: Noah dies at nine hundred and fifty.

notes.text: The frame of chapter 5, closing the last life of that genealogy.

reading: and [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the days|the days, the day-breaks, the times]] of [[name:Νωε]] nine hundred fifty years, and [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]].
